pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Beta APIs for DRA in 1.32.

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123687, #127386

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
The core functionality of Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) got promoted to beta. No action is required when *upgrading*, the previous v1alpha3 API is still supported, so existing deployments and DRA drivers based on v1alpha3 continue to work. *Downgrading* from 1.32 to 1.31 with DRA resources in the cluster (resourceclaims, resourceclaimtemplates, deviceclasses, resourceslices) is *not* supported because the new v1beta1 is used as storage version and not readable by 1.31.
```

issue_context.title: DRA: beta: CEL validation
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

At the moment, `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/namedresources/cel/compile.go` uses 1.0 as version for everything in its CEL environment to grant the alpha API CEL expressions access to things defined in the 1.30 release. We need to change that to the real version before promotion to beta.

### Why is this needed?

New expression must not use CEL expressions which become invalid on a downgrade, so only features already available in the previous release are valid.
comments: Once https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123687 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123516 are merged to the same branch, a [RemovedVersion](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46f017a90b54b5abfc0a66a6ecf19e304aa7da95/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/environment/environment.go#L177) can be added to the DRA specific implementation to prevent future versions from enabling both copies of the library.

Hello @pohly @jpbetz 
I would like to send a gentle remind. The code freeze is starting 02:00 UTC Friday November 8th 2024 (about 3 weeks from now), and while there is still time, we want to ensure that each PR has a chance to be merged on time.
As the PR is tagged for 1.32, is it still planned for this release?
Thank you!

review_comments: Thank you for adding the "as JSON" part! ❤️
It's the small details which make error messages useful :grin:

I added a comment about "Downgrades from 1.32 to 1.31 are not supported" to the release note.

I am not sure whether that warrants an `ACTION REQUIRED: when downgrading from 1.32 to 1.31, delete ..." ?

In order to support serialized data, I thought we don't actually REMOVE old APIs.  But it does look like we remove old ALPHA APIs - but only sometimes.  e.g. discovery/v1a1 was removed but admissionregistration/v1alpha1 still has VAP.

I am not sure this part is OK.  If someone uses the beta, and then rolls back, we should not penalize them.

They roll back to an alpha where we can't fix some knows bugs because our cherry-pick guidelines treat fixes for off-by-default alpha features as [not eligible](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-release/cherry-picks.md#what-kind-of-prs-are-good-for-cherry-picks). I think admins who need to roll back shouldn't expect the feature to work and are better of disabling workloads.

is it ok that existing DRA plugins will fail? Let's mention it in release notes
They don't fail: they report "1.0.0" because a version was required by 1.31, and then `validateSupportedServices` falls back to using the alpha API exactly to prevent them from failing:

```
	// Fall back to alpha if necessary because
	// plugins at that time didn't advertise gRPC services.
	if chosenService == "" {
		chosenService = drapbv1alpha4.NodeService
	}

	return chosenService, nil
```
To verify, I ran the DRA E2E tests from Kubernetes 1.31  (minus classic DRA, minus one slow test)  against a cluster using this PR where the resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3 is enabled. This covers version skew between a client (e2e.test) and the apiserver as well as version skew between a DRA driver (the test driver from 1.31) and kubelet. All passed.

I then replaced kubelet with kubelet from 1.31 and ran the E2E tests from this PR. This covers version skew between kubelet and the control plane. However, that fails because drivers now don't provide a semantic version in the "supported versions", which causes kubelet from 1.31 to reject registation:
  
```
              {
                  FullMethod: "/pluginregistration.Registration/NotifyRegistrationStatus",
                  Request: 
                      error: 'RegisterPlugin error -- plugin validation failed with err: invalid versions
                        of plugin dra-8953.k8s.io: none of the versions are supported: could not find a
                        highest supported version from versions ([v1beta1.DRAPlugin]) reported: illegal
                        version string "v1beta1.DRAPlugin"',
                  Response: 
                      null,
                  Err: <*errors.errorString | 0xc000e10a90>{
                      s: "failed registration process: RegisterPlugin error -- plugin validation failed with err: invalid versions of plugin dra-8953.k8s.io: none of the versions are supported: could not find a highest supported version from versions ([v1beta1.DRAPlugin]) reported: illegal version string \"v1beta1.DRAPlugin\"",
                  },
              },
```

We could tweak the helper code a bit: if a DRA driver is configured to *only* enable the alpha gRPC server, then we can report "1.0.0" instead of the (according to the new rules) correct "v1alpha3.Node". Then such a driver works in this version skew scenario. Whether any DRA vendor will *support* that is a different question, but it seems useful to have the ability. I added it in a separate commit ("DRA driver: support kubelet 1.31").

More important for DRA in general is that version skew between kubelet and the control plane works as intended, which will become important for future Kubernetes releases. Combining an alpha-level kubelet with a beta-level control plane seems unlikely. Beta-level kubelet from 1.32 with beta-level control plane from 1.33 is more likely.
At some point we will need to remove this logic. Maybe in separate PR we need to write a warning when this fallback was chosen.

Agreed, this is temporary. Once all DRA drivers are known to support 1.32, we can remove it. It's support for an alpha, so we can do that from one release to the next, although it won't hurt to give it more time.

Could we revisit the decision to leave this feature gate off by default in beta?

Usually feature-gates graduating to beta are turned on by default. However, the decision to keep this feature gate turned off was made because the corresponding `resource.k8s.io API` group needed to actually make use of this feature will also be turned off by default (as per the [policy for beta API groups](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/#api-versioning)).

On the surface, it seems logical to make the feature gate disabled-by-default if the API group is disabled-by-default. The problem, however, is that most managed Kubernetes services (notably GKE and EKS) **_don't_** allow users to enable beta feature gates, but **_do_** allow users to enable beta API groups. 

By making the feature-gate disabled-by-default we are basically making it so that no one can actually use this feature in managed Kubernetes environments even if they choose to enable the `resource.k8s.io` API group.

Are there potential downsides to enabling this feature-gate by default (just like most other beta feature gates) that I am missing?
/cc @johnbelamaric @thockin @pohly
Enabling the feature by default would fix AllAlpha=true clusters (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127511#issuecomment-2451910268).

we went through this in other threads and I specifically with the ServiceCIDR feature that I'm driving.  The decision was to not allow the beta APIs to be turned on by default, consequently it was not possible to me to find a way to enable the feature that depends on the api groups, @deads2k and @liggitt are the persons to convince here

> (notably GKE and EKS) don't allow users to enable beta feature gates, but do allow users to enable beta API groups.

GKE allows to enable the feature gates based on the api groups, I just did it recently and I think this will be the same for DRA https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/release-notes-new-features#October_04_2024, so this should not be a problem at least in the GKE side, but I don't see why EKS can not do the same

What Antonio said is my feeling.  Don't get me wrong - the fact that we have two different enablements is high on my list of things that make me irrationally angry, but I don't think having it half-on-by-default is better

I find my "it's a better user experience" argument pretty convincing - see commit message in the new "WIP: DRA: enable feature by default".

> consequently it was not possible to me to find a way to enable the feature that depends on the api groups

I may have found a way. Whether it is worth the extra complexity and/or a terrible hack remains to be seen - please have a look.

Let me quote the argument so that we are all on the same page:

```
First, the user experience is a bit better. With feature gate on + group off,
they are able to create pods which reference claims or claim templates, but
not those claims and claim templates. The pods then remain pending, with an
obvious explanation from the scheduler (along the lines of "claim not
found"). With feature gate off, the usual "drop disabled fields" logic kicks
in and the pods get scheduled without the additional resources, which is
a less obvious failure mode and potentially wasting resources on the node
for a pod that is likely to go into a crash loop.
```

So with "feature gate on", uses get early feedback in the pod status and events. With "feature gate off", they don't get that and have to figure out why a pod fails on a node.

> we also have beta API's off by default decision right? 

Yes, and we'll follow that no matter what.

I think this was more correct before - what motivated this change?

Some of the failure messages don't include the key text, for example when `validateDriverName = corevalidation.ValidateCSIDriverName` calls `field.TooLong`. The result is then this failure:

```
spec.devices[1].basic.attributes: Too long: must have at most 63 bytes
```

This looks like a problem with the map as a whole, but it's only a problem with one entry. There's nothing that tells the user which entry in the map has that problem. This is an area where `listType=map` has an advantage because it can easily include the index and the field.

This particular failure doesn't even give the actual length. Clearly driver name validation could be done better; perhaps I should fork `corevalidation.ValidateCSIDriverName` and do that.

But that then would have to be ensured for all key validation functions. Extending the field path seemed like a better way of ensuring that the information is guaranteed to be there. The downside is that if the key is really long, it all gets included. However, that problem also occurs when it's too long and we then call 
`validateItem(item, fldPath.Key(string(key))` - perhaps `fldPath.Key` or this code here should truncate?

The other motivation was that if some subset of the key fails validation, we get information about that part,  but not the key as a whole:

```
spec.devices[1].basic.attributes: Required value: the domain must not be empty
spec.devices[1].basic.attributes: Required value: the C identifier must not be empty
```

With this change, we get instead:
```
spec.devices[1].basic.attributes[/]: Required value: the domain must not be empty
spec.devices[1].basic.attributes[/]: Required value: the C identifier must not be empty
```

This points towards yet another potential improvement: instead of comparing errors, the tests perhaps should compare error texts. Then we verify and can review what the user sees. Other validation tests don't bother with checking what error(s) occur, others compare some of the error fields, but not all. I'm not sure whether the exact type of the error matters anywhere, but at least the error text is relevant, so IMHO it should be checked.
